Beam tracks image the He-3 target

run_145 · stat090_0000 · arm A (det3) · nTOF partner 224670 · 2026-08-12 · PRELIMINARY

The waveform-first reconstruction, run for the first time on a fully nTOF-matched beam run, back-projects arm A's tracks to a compact source at the origin — the He-3 target is imaged. The reconstructed angle follows the point-source expectation tan θ = u / 235 mm across the plane, and the residual scale factor gives the first in-situ drift velocity at beam conditions: v ≈ 36.1 µm/ns, 15 % below the clean-gas Magboltz prior of 42.6. A second step — requiring an in-time hit in the SiPM wall segment the track points to and in the plastic bar behind it — confirms 58 % of predictable tracks externally, and the extrapolated tracks land in the correct 100 mm wall group with the segment ordering reproduced exactly.

What ran

run_145 (Aug 5, production statistics at the run_67 optimum: drift 700 V on all four chambers, resist A540/B540/C525/D520 V, Ar/iC4H10 90/10, 20 samples × 60 ns) is the only last-week run whose every sub-run carries complete nTOF matching — all three segments joined to nTOF run 224670 at ~95 % efficiency by the slim pipeline. Tracks come from the frozen MPGD26 wft/ chain (multi-track HEAD, single-track output bit-identical to the bench-validated code; the test suite passes on the analysis machine), driven by ntof_tracking/wft_beam.py with the bench→beam calibration transfer of PLAN_08: the impulse template and resistive-sharing kernel carry over as chamber hardware, the DAQ constants are replaced by run_145's, and v_drift starts as a Magboltz prior — which the imaging then measures. The per-event nTOF record is joined on eventId straight from the slim ntof_hits file; requiring a same-arm SiPM-wall hit is the purity cut.

The in-situ calibration

Positions never depend on v_drift; angles scale as 1/v. A ray from the origin crossing the strip plane at u must have tan θ = u/L exactly, so every inclined track measures the angle scale directly: ki = (ui/L)/tan θi.

quantityvaluecomment
v prior (Magboltz, clean 90/10, 233 V/cm)42.6 µm/nsbundle as seeded
v in-situ, imaging (arm A)36.1 µm/nsk = 1.18, |u| < 130 mm
bench wet-gas reference at this field23.3 µm/nsAr/iso 95/5 + H2O curve

36.1 sits between the clean-gas prediction and the wet bench curve — consistent with mildly wet gas after a month of flow, but deliberately quoted as an effective angle scale: the 20-sample readout window truncates the deepest columns and compresses large angles (the window-ablation prediction), and that compression is partially absorbed into k. For pointing and imaging purposes the effective scale is the right thing to use; separating true v from truncation needs the per-angle treatment.

Step 2 — the wall + plastic pointing coincidence

Every DREAM trigger is a same-arm SiPM-wall AND plastic coincidence, and the slim record says which wall segment (4 groups of 100 mm, 96 mm past the strips) and which plastic bar (two 200 mm bars, ~188 mm past the strips) fired. The second step extrapolates each track to both planes and requires an in-time hit (−100 < Δt < +60 ns) in the predicted segment AND the predicted bar — per-track external confirmation on two lever arms, using the channel ordering measured on run_79 (descending; detn pair 0 at most-positive u). Of 5,992 tracks whose extrapolation lands on the wall and a bar, 3,450 (58 %) pass both.

With and without the SiPM requirement

How much work is the nTOF side actually doing? Left: every reconstructed two-plane track. Right: only events whose slim record has a same-arm SiPM wall hit. The requirement removes ~20 % of tracks (8,484 → 6,727) — the DREAM trigger is an OR over the four arms, so that fraction of arm-A tracks was triggered by another arm — and both selections show the same target structure, the matched one modestly cleaner. The imaging does not depend on the nTOF match; the match buys purity and, through Step 2, per-track external confirmation.

The event, from the waveforms up

The same displays the run_79 preliminary pass introduced, regenerated on run_145 with the frozen code. Event 36245 is a "golden" pick: both planes quality-ok, wall AND plastic tags in the arm, the extrapolation inside both fired elements, and the ray passing 1.1 mm from the beam axis at the capsule.

D's high statistics (46k reconstructed events — twice the other arms) match its known occupancy. The v ordering A ≈ D > C is not yet a gas statement: C's number is bundle-limited and B's field is not nominal, so the clean gas-chain reading needs the C recalibration and the D mapping check first.

What this does not show (yet)

  • The axial (Y) image is inconclusive. The y-plane pointing correlation is flat and the Y-profile of near-axis tracks shows no clear capsule concentration — y-plane angle quality and the in-plane offsets need work before the second imaging coordinate is real.
  • In-plane offsets are un-surveyed. The strip-map zero per arm is provisional (geometry caveat since PLAN_01); the ~5 mm off-axis ridge in Fig 2 is its likely signature. The natural next step is a two-parameter (u0, k) fit per arm — the imaging constrains both.
  • One sub-run. All four arms are reconstructed on sub-run 0000 (fleet table above); sub-run 0001 is staged and unprocessed. The D in-plane mirror and the C recalibration are the open per-arm items.
  • Single-k calibration. First-order only; the |u| > 130 compression is excluded, not corrected.
Caveat — resolved to a known, small effect (updated the same evening). The June cosmic-bench discrepancy flagged on the day of writing was localized: the frozen reconstruction stopped applying the bundles' per-plane angle-mapping constants (w0/kw), a sub-degree angle bias per detector plane (arctan(w0/v) reproduces the fleet's bias table). On this arm's x plane the constants are tiny (w0x = −0.004, kwx = 1.006): applying them post-hoc moved the in-situ v by 0.6 % (36.3 → 36.1 µm/ns), inside quoted precision, and all figures on this page now carry the correction. Arms B/C inherit larger constants (0.3–0.7°) and their imaging applies the same correction. The code fix (restore the field on the bundle class, then re-apply in the fit) is owned by the bench-side sessions.

Archive — the run_79 preliminaries (July 31 daily summary)

The visuals below are the first waveform-first beam pass, shown at the July 31 daily summary: run_79 arm A with the pre-freeze code generation and the transferred (not in-situ) calibration. They are kept here as the context this page supersedes — run_145 above repeats the same checks on the frozen code with full nTOF matching and better numbers (wall pointing 51–71 % inside vs 45–58 % then). Treat run_79 numbers as historical.

ntof_tracking/wft_beam.py (bundle + reco per arm) and ntof_tracking/run145_target_imaging.py (pointing, image, k-scan) at repo HEAD; data under x17match/ on the desktop, slim products from out_224670. Frozen code commit in CODE_COMMIT.txt next to the deployed package.
